svg.aria-label: Meet the simulated buyers: Yash Malhotra, 42, an app-cab owner-driver in Pune and one simulated person from the 3,000-person run, answers his life interview (Realme 9 Pro on Jio prepaid at 349 rupees, lost 6,000 rupees to a crypto course, asks his wife, his mother and a stall partner before buying). His persona fills in, then his decision card: says yes to a free trial, cheap price, family plan and a Hindi coach; walks away from a card needed upfront, hidden charges and over-promising ads; trusts 4+ star reviews, clear prices and family opinion; says he would exercise in waiting time but long shifts make it unlikely. The stereotype guard checks that no two people in an audience share a job and a city, and the next buyers appear.

svg.text: Every person is written, interviewed and given a decision card before any test.

g.text: What phone do you use, and what is your data plan like?
Realme 9 Pro, Jio prepaid ₹349, 2 GB a day.
Tell me about a time you got scammed.
₹6,000 went on a crypto course. Now I read reviews.
Who do you ask before spending real money?
Pooja, my wife, my mother, and Santosh at the stall.
What annoys you most in ads?
Over-promising, long unskippable ads, card upfront.
free trial, cheap price, family plan, a
reviews with 4+ stars, clear prices, family
says 15 minutes in waiting time; long shifts
Stereotype guard: no two people in an audience share both a job and a city.

svg.text: Yash is one simulated person from the README's 3,000-person run, abridged.
